source.title: Gradient Descent with Early Stopping is Provably Robust to Label Noise for Overparameterized Neural Networks
source.authors: Ming-Chen Li; M. Soltanolkotabi; Samet Oymak

record.file_problem: Full paper text is supplied, including results, experiments, proofs, and references.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether overparameterized networks can fit corrupted labels yet retain predictive performance under early stopping, using label-corruption experiments and theoretical guarantees rather than the original random-label memorization and natural-label comparison.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own results on fitting randomly corrupted labels, early stopping, test accuracy, and measured distance from initialization. Cited results about fitting pure noise and other prior work are not rows. Figure values without reported numerical values are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: Figure 1a tests V1's coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in a new MNIST architecture. The early-stopping experiments and clustered-data theory principally address label-noise robustness, a different claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors establish robustness to bounded label corruption with early-stopped gradient descent under clustered-data assumptions, complement it with distance-from-initialization lower bounds, and present corroborating experiments. Perfectly clustered data require no early stopping. They explicitly distinguish their robustness results from generalization in the traditional sense.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments train with random label corruption and early stopping, and the theory uses a clusterable-data model; the original claim's core test compares fitting fixed random labels with generalization on natural labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Early stopping versus many iterations; corruption fraction; clustered-data input noise and cluster structure.

fits_no_version.finding: Early stopping preserves high MNIST test accuracy despite substantial partial label corruption; clustered-data theorems establish related recovery guarantees.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterized networks can resist partial label noise when gradient descent is stopped early, under suitable data conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Corrupted-label fitting requires greater movement from initialization, and prolonged training can erase the separation between clean and corrupted training losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distance from initialization and training duration distinguish early label-noise robustness from later memorization.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: The empirical demonstrations do not directly compare memorization of fixed random labels against generalization on natural labels. Several plotted outcomes have no numerical values in the text. The theoretical guarantees rely on a clusterable dataset model, a one-hidden-layer scalar-output network, and specified corruption and input-noise conditions; the authors call for extension to deeper architectures and more complex data models.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure 1 and Figure 3 plotted numerical values are not transcribed because the text does not state them.

untested.parts: Exact chance-level held-out accuracy with fully random labels is not established by the supplied readable results. The named original architectures and datasets are not replicated.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers under comparable tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Early-stopping benefits do not limit V1: V1 does not claim that memorization and generalization must occur simultaneously on partially corrupted data or at every stopping time. No verdict is warranted from the robustness-only rows. Figure values omitted by the reader are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests natural-label predictive performance under random label corruption and reports eventual fitting of corrupted labels in some settings, but does not test fixed random labels with held-out accuracy at chance, nor the named small Inception, AlexNet, MLP, or Inception V3 comparisons.
Widening beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error are not tested.
Convolutional versus fully connected performance and local connectivity are not tested as comparisons.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons are not tested.
Batch-size effects on generalization are not tested.
Dropout and its effects on held-out error are not tested.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap are not measured.
Removing memorized examples and retraining is not tested.

rows.subject: 4 layer neural network consisting of two convolution layers followed by two fully-connected layers
rows.size_stated: 4.8 million trainable parameters; convolution widths 64 and 128 kernels; fully-connected outputs 256 and 10
rows.operation_detail: Train on MNIST with varying fractions of training labels randomly corrupted; evaluate training accuracy, test accuracy, and training accuracy against true labels.

conditions.value: various amounts of random corruption; figure shows 0% to 100%

rows.measure: training accuracy on corrupted labels, test accuracy, and training accuracy relative to true labels
rows.note: The text says the model achieved near-perfect fitting to corrupted data after 200 epochs and that test accuracy and true-label training accuracy degraded with many iterations; no exact values are provided in the text.
rows.check: The text establishes near-perfect corrupted-label fitting after 200 epochs and includes the uncorrupted-label condition. Exact test accuracies, including chance-level performance at 100% corruption, cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text. Split the combined measures and corruption conditions into separate rows.

rows.subject: 4 layer neural network consisting of two convolution layers followed by two fully-connected layers
rows.size_stated: 4.8 million trainable parameters; convolution widths 64 and 128 kernels; fully-connected outputs 256 and 10
rows.stage_stated: trained with early stopping; stopping iteration not stated
rows.operation_detail: Train on MNIST with varying fractions of training labels randomly corrupted and stop after a few iterations.

conditions.value: various amounts of random corruption; figure shows through 90%

rows.measure: training accuracy on corrupted labels, test accuracy, and training accuracy relative to true labels
rows.note: The text reports that test accuracy remains high under significant corruption and that training accuracy against true labels stays around 100% even at 50% corruption; exact values are not stated.
rows.check: High accuracy despite partial label corruption under early stopping measures noise robustness. This stopping recipe does not demonstrate near-perfect random-label fitting, so it does not establish V1's coexistence.

rows.subject: LENET model
rows.stage_stated: trained; optimizer and stopping rule not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measure training accuracy and training loss against relative distance from initialization under different label-corruption levels.
rows.measure: training accuracy and training loss versus relative distance from initialization
rows.note: The authors state that distance from initialization increases gracefully with more corruption; the plotted values are not given in the text.
rows.check: The recorded outcome concerns distance from initialization versus training fit, without held-out accuracy. The architecture is ambiguous: the caption calls it LENET, whereas Section 3 calls it the Figure 1 model.

rows.subject: Resnet-20
rows.size_stated: around 270,000 parameters in the CIFAR-10 model
rows.stage_stated: trained with gradient descent; stopping iteration not stated
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 with random label corruption and compare clean-example and corrupted-example loss distributions.
rows.measure: cross-entropy loss distributions for clean and corrupted training examples
rows.note: The text describes approximate separation, not a held-out test-error or test-accuracy measurement.
rows.check: Training-loss separation measures label-noise robustness, not V1's memorization/generalization comparison. Figure 4 explicitly specifies early stopping; add that condition.

rows.subject: Resnet-20
rows.size_stated: around 270,000 parameters in the CIFAR-10 model
rows.stage_stated: trained with gradient descent; stopping iteration not stated
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 with random label corruption and compare clean-example and corrupted-example loss distributions.
rows.measure: cross-entropy loss distributions for clean and corrupted training examples
rows.value: clean-data training loss increases and distributions begin to overlap
rows.note: The study reports a weaker distinction at 50% corruption; it does not report held-out test performance for this experiment.
rows.check: Overlap between training-loss distributions does not measure any listed version. Figure 4 explicitly specifies early stopping; add that condition.

rows.subject: one-hidden layer network with k=1000 hidden units
rows.size_stated: k=1000 hidden units; n=400 samples; d=20
rows.stage_stated: gradient descent; early stopping at iteration 80 and later training to iteration 4500
rows.operation_detail: Train on a generated two-class clustered dataset with 30% corrupted labels; track classification errors and clean/corrupted sample loss distributions.
rows.measure: training error relative to clean labels and corrupted labels; least-squares loss distributions
rows.value: at iteration 4500 the model overfits; clean and corrupted loss distributions overlap
rows.note: The figure caption and text report early good classification followed by overfitting later. The data are generated from a clustered model, not natural labels, and no held-out test accuracy is reported.
rows.check: This synthetic-data experiment reports training-label recovery followed by overfitting, without natural-label held-out performance. Separate the iteration-80 and iteration-4500 outcomes.

rows.subject: one-hidden layer network with k hidden units
rows.size_stated: k exceeds the theorem's stated bound; bound depends on K, cluster covariance, and constants
rows.operation_detail: Theorem guarantees correct predictions on the support neighborhoods of clusters despite bounded label corruption.
rows.measure: classification against ground-truth labels for inputs within ε0 of cluster centers
rows.value: predicts the true label function for all such inputs with stated probability
rows.note: This is a theoretical guarantee under the paper's clusterable data model, not an empirical natural-image held-out test.
rows.check: The theorem guarantees label recovery on cluster neighborhoods under bounded corruption. It does not establish that the same recipe fits fully random labels.

rows.subject: one-hidden layer network with k hidden units
rows.size_stated: k satisfies the theorem's stated bound
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 8.13 bounds error against ground-truth labels under clusterable noisy data.
rows.measure: per-sample normalized ℓ2 error and number of prediction errors against true labels
rows.value: error bound and prediction-error fraction bounded by expressions in Theorem 8.13
rows.note: The guarantee depends on cluster assumptions and input-noise conditions; it is not a random-label test-accuracy experiment.
rows.check: The theorem bounds recovery of ground-truth labels under clustered corruption, rather than testing any listed version. Its value should state the bounds instead of referring generically to expressions.

rows.subject: one-hidden layer network with k hidden units
rows.operation_detail: Lower-bound distance from initialization needed for a network to fit two nearby inputs with separated labels.
rows.measure: minimum ∥W−W0∥F required to fit both labels
rows.note: This is a bound on parameter distance for fitting a corrupted-label pattern, not a direct test-generalization measurement.
rows.check: A parameter-distance lower bound is not a memorization/generalization comparison. The theorem also requires the candidate weights to lie within a stated Frobenius-distance neighborhood of initialization; that condition is omitted.

rows.subject: one-hidden layer network with k hidden units
rows.operation_detail: Theorem guarantees prediction of correct labels on perfectly clustered examples under label corruption.
rows.measure: classification on all samples against ground-truth labels
rows.value: network predicts the correct label for all samples
rows.note: The paper explicitly states that in the perfectly clustered case there is no need for early stopping and the network does not overfit even after many iterations.
rows.check: Correct-label recovery for perfectly clustered inputs does not test V1. Identical inputs with conflicting labels cannot be interpolated; the absence of overfitting here does not challenge random-label fitting on distinct images.

relationships.condition: MNIST four-layer convolutional model trained for 200 epochs with Adadelta; qualitative coexistence component
relationships.reason: R1's corruption sweep includes natural and fully randomized labels and reports near-perfect training fit alongside the natural-label test comparison; support is qualitative because test values are unreadable.
relationships.display_finding: The reported near-perfect fitting across label corruption and paired natural-label test performance remain unverified from the available source.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: early-stopped models and the paper's clusterable data settings
reader_labels.reason: The study reports robustness to corrupted labels and high test accuracy in its MNIST early-stopping experiment, with theoretical guarantees on clustered data, but does not test the version's fixed random-label versus natural-label held-out comparison (R2, R7, R8, R10).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MNIST model trained for many iterations under corrupted labels
reader_labels.reason: The model reaches near-perfect corrupted-label fit, while the text reports degradation in test accuracy and training accuracy against true labels, consistent with overfitting after prolonged training (R1).
